specs.anchorText: We define the corruption, the forward process, with no learning at all.
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background, generous margins. A gentle two-panel comic strip read left to right. Left panel: a friendly little robot uses a tiny watering can to sprinkle grey sandy static over a cheerful sandcastle shaped like a cat, the castle slowly dissolving into a flat pile of speckled grey grains; a small orange arrow points rightward. Right panel: a second friendly robot, patient and focused, uses a tiny brush to sweep the grey grains away one speckle at a time, the cat-shaped sandcastle re-forming crisp and complete; a small green arrow points leftward. The two robots mirror each other. The style is friendly and approachable like an XKCD-inspired infographic meets Kurzgesagt, soft palette of warm orange, sage green, and dusty blue, expressive but minimal characters, no visual clutter. No text or lettering anywhere in the image. The humor is gentle: ruining a picture on purpose so the ruin becomes a road map back. Keep the composition simple and focused on the destroy-then-rebuild metaphor.
specs.alt: A two-panel cartoon: one friendly robot sprinkles grey static over a cat-shaped sandcastle until it dissolves into grains (the fixed forward noising process), and a mirror-image robot brushes the grains away grain by grain to rebuild the same cat castle (the learned reverse denoising process), capturing how diffusion turns generation into repeated denoising.
specs.caption: Destroy then rebuild: drown a picture in static on purpose, learn to sweep that static away one grain at a time, and ruin becomes a road map back to a brand-new image.

specs.anchorText: many easy steps, not one hard leap
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background, generous margins. Split scene comparing two routes up to the same goal. On the left, a small friendly robot strains and sweats at the bottom of a single enormous sheer cliff labeled with nothing, trying and failing to leap to the top in one impossible jump, looking exhausted. On the right, the same cheerful robot calmly climbs a gentle wide staircase of many small steps toward the same hilltop where a finished framed picture of a smiling cat waits; on the lowest steps the picture-in-progress is a blurry grey blob, and as the steps rise the blob resolves into a clear cat, coarse shape first then fine detail. Soft palette of warm orange, sage green, and dusty blue, expressive minimal characters, no clutter. No text or lettering in the image. Gentle humor in the contrast between the impossible leap and the easy stroll. Keep the composition focused on the one-hard-leap versus many-easy-steps metaphor.
specs.alt: A cartoon contrasting a tired robot failing to leap up a sheer cliff in one jump with the same robot calmly climbing a gentle staircase of many small steps, where a blurry grey blob on the low steps gradually resolves into a clear cat picture near the top, showing why diffusion takes many easy denoising steps instead of one impossible leap and learns coarse structure before fine detail.
specs.caption: Diffusion trades one impossible prediction for a long chain of trivial ones: coarse shape resolves on the early steps, fine texture on the last, so the model only ever solves an easy problem.

specs.anchorText: the only unknown standing between us and a generator
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background, generous margins. A friendly cartoon hiker robot stands in soft rolling fog on a gentle landscape of grassy hills, holding up a glowing compass whose single arrow always points toward the nearest uphill direction. The arrow guides the robot up the slope toward the rounded summits of two cozy hills (the modes of a density), away from the flat foggy valley. Small faint matching arrows dot the hillsides, all pointing uphill toward the peaks, suggesting a field of directions. Soft palette of sage green hills, dusty blue fog, warm orange compass glow, expressive friendly character, minimal clutter. No text or lettering in the image. The gentle idea: the score is a compass that always shows which way density rises. Keep the composition simple and focused on the uphill-compass metaphor.
specs.alt: A cartoon hiker robot in light fog holds a glowing compass whose arrow always points uphill, guiding it toward the rounded summits of two hills while faint matching arrows across the slopes all point toward the peaks, illustrating the score function as the gradient of log-density that everywhere points toward the modes of the data and is the only unknown the reverse process must estimate.
specs.caption: The score is the only compass the reverse process needs: at every noise level it points toward higher density, and following it uphill walks pure static back toward the modes of the data.

specs.anchorText: why not walk in a straight line?
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background, generous margins. Two friendly robot travelers leave the same starting town (a small cloud of grey static) heading to the same destination town (a tidy little house representing data). One robot follows a long winding curvy road that loops back and forth across the hills, dotted with many tiny milestone markers showing it must take many small careful steps. The other robot strolls along a perfectly straight ruler-like road directly to the house, with only two or three milestone markers, arriving relaxed. The straight-road robot cheerfully holds up a ruler. Soft palette of warm orange winding road, sage green straight road, dusty blue sky, expressive minimal characters, no clutter. No text or lettering in the image. Gentle humor: why wander when you can go straight. Keep the composition focused on the curved-many-steps versus straight-few-steps metaphor.
specs.alt: A cartoon showing two robots traveling from a town of grey static to a house representing data: one takes a long winding curvy road dotted with many small step markers, the other strolls down a perfectly straight ruler-like road with only a few markers, illustrating how flow matching and rectified flow straighten the generative path so a sampler can reach data in very few steps instead of many.
specs.caption: Diffusion inherits a winding road from noise to data that demands many steps; flow matching hands the model a ruler and draws a straight line, which is why rectified-flow systems sample well in a handful of steps.

specs.anchorText: do the diffusion in a compressed
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background, generous margins. A three-room cartoon workshop building shown in cutaway, read left to right. Left room: a friendly encoder robot feeds a big detailed landscape painting into a shrinking machine that squeezes it down into a small neat folded map (the latent). Middle room, the largest and busiest: several little painter robots happily work on that small folded map at a tiny easel, sweeping grey static off it step by step, while a separate text-reader robot in a side booth whispers hints through a speaking tube into the room (cross-attention conditioning). Right room: a decoder robot feeds the finished small map into an unfolding machine that blooms it back into a full detailed landscape painting, done only once. The middle small-map room is clearly cozy and cheap compared to the big paintings on the ends. Soft palette of dusty blue, sage green middle room, warm orange machines, purple text booth, expressive minimal characters, no clutter. No text or lettering in the image. Keep the composition focused on the compress, dream-in-the-small-space, then render-once pipeline.
specs.alt: A cutaway cartoon workshop in three rooms: an encoder robot squeezes a large detailed painting into a small folded map, painter robots denoise that small map step by step in a cozy middle room while a text-reader robot whispers hints through a tube (cross-attention), and a decoder robot unfolds the finished small map back into a full painting just once, illustrating the two-stage latent diffusion pipeline of Stable Diffusion that runs the costly diffusion in a compact latent space.
specs.caption: Latent diffusion compresses the image into a small map, does all the expensive dreaming in that cheap space (with text whispered in through cross-attention), and only renders back to full pixels once, the trick that put Stable Diffusion on a consumer GPU.

specs.anchorText: they subtract the full predicted noise at once and produce a blurry average image
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background, generous margins. A friendly but overeager robot stands at an easel having just yanked off all the grey static from a noisy canvas in one big impatient sweep with a giant squeegee, holding the wad of removed static in one hand. The result on the canvas is a disappointing smeary blurry ghost of an average face, foggy and featureless, with a small sweat-drop and a confused expression on the robot. Beside it, a small calm thumbnail shows the correct gentle approach: a tidy robot peeling off just a thin calibrated sliver of static, leaving a crisp clear picture. Soft palette of warm orange, sage green, dusty blue and muted grey for the blur, expressive minimal characters, no clutter. No text or lettering in the image. Gentle humor in the overeager robot's blunder. Keep the composition focused on the all-at-once-subtraction-makes-mush failure versus the calibrated-fraction fix.
specs.alt: A cartoon of an overeager robot that wiped off all the predicted noise from a canvas in one big squeegee sweep and got only a blurry featureless average face, beside a small thumbnail of a calm robot peeling off just a thin calibrated sliver of noise to leave a crisp picture, illustrating the common implementation bug where subtracting the full predicted noise at once collapses samples into a blurry average instead of advancing one careful step.
specs.caption: The denoiser predicts all the noise back to the clean image, but the reverse step must subtract only a calibrated fraction; rip it all off at once and you get a blurry average instead of a sample.
